title: Ideal Gaussian tests have less than 29 percent power for 90-ppm attenuation in two selected Kepler dips of KIC 8462852
abstract: We test the information available to distinguish a constant 90-ppm periodic source from a uniformly dimmed source during two known dips of KIC 8462852. We use Kepler release 25 times and formal flux errors. We fix the known frequency at 1.1377 cycles per day. Four loss profiles use smoothing widths of 0.1 to 0.8 day. At a 5 percent false-positive rate, an ideal test with known baseline, signal phase and loss profile has at most 17.4 percent power in quarter 8 and 28.4 percent in quarter 16. Unknown spline baselines reduce power further. Exact linear algebra and 2000 Gaussian draws per fitted design check the method. These are conditional sensitivity limits, not tests of the observed source position. They assume independent Gaussian errors at the archived error scale and do not include detector noise or loss-profile uncertainty. No new source or planet is found. Code, input hashes, aggregate results and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Ideal power at 90 ppm and amplitude needed for 95 percent power. Solid lines use the best phase; dotted lines use the worst phase. Known dip permits a fitted constant and coherent sinusoid. Other points allow an unknown cubic spline baseline. Independent Gaussian errors at the archived scale are assumed.

citations.reason: Prior attenuation-fit failure motivates this separate information and power test.
Supplies the fixed frequency and earlier source test.
Shows that a fixed periodic shape across quarters is a restrictive assumption.
Provides context on detector and aperture limits for these two dips.
